title: MLOps
shortDefinition: The practice of applying DevOps principles to AI model development and deployment lifecycles.
definition: MLOps (Machine Learning Operations) is the practice of applying DevOps principles — automation, continuous integration, monitoring, and reproducibility — to the full machine learning model lifecycle, from data preparation and model training through deployment, monitoring, and retraining. MLOps transforms AI model development from a one-time research exercise into a reliable, repeatable, and maintainable engineering discipline — the organizational and technical infrastructure that determines whether AI capabilities stay reliably operational after initial deployment.

sections.title: What MLOps encompasses in practice
sections.description: MLOps spans data pipeline management, experiment tracking, continuous training, deployment automation, and production monitoring.

content.text: MLOps spans several connected disciplines: data pipeline management (ensuring training data remains current and high-quality over time), experiment tracking and model versioning (recording what data, code, and configuration produced each model version, enabling reproducibility and rollback), continuous training pipelines (automating model retraining on schedules or drift-triggered signals), deployment automation (reliable, reproducible model promotion from development through staging to production), and production monitoring (detecting drift, accuracy degradation, or serving infrastructure failures before they significantly impact users).

items: Data pipeline management — keep training data current and high-quality.
Experiment tracking — record data, code, and configuration for each version.
Model versioning — enable reproducibility and rollback.
Continuous training — automate retraining based on schedules or drift.
Deployment automation — reliable promotion through environments.
Production monitoring — detect drift, degradation, and infrastructure issues.

content.title: The key insight
content.text: MLOps transforms AI model development from a one-time research exercise into a reliable, repeatable engineering discipline.

sections.title: Why MLOps matters beyond the initial deployment

content.text: A significant share of AI projects successfully deliver an initial model but fail to maintain it reliably over time — accuracy gradually degrades as real-world data patterns shift from what the model was trained on, pipeline failures silently corrupt data quality, and model updates require fragile manual processes that don't reproduce consistently. MLOps addresses these ongoing operational challenges by building the same rigor into AI model lifecycle management that software engineering has developed for application code — reducing the risk that a successful AI project gradually becomes a liability.

items: Accuracy degradation — drift as data patterns shift over time.
Pipeline failures — silent corruption of data quality.
Fragile updates — manual processes that don't reproduce consistently.
Operational rigor — applying software engineering discipline to AI.
Liability prevention — keeping successful AI projects from becoming problems.

items.question: What's the difference between MLOps and DevOps?
items.answer: DevOps applies to software application lifecycle management; MLOps extends these principles to the specific challenges of machine learning model lifecycle management, which introduces additional concerns (data quality, model drift, experiment reproducibility) that standard DevOps tooling doesn't fully address.

items.question: Does MLOps require a dedicated team, or can it be handled by existing engineering teams?
items.answer: This depends on model portfolio size and update frequency; smaller portfolios can often be managed by engineering teams with appropriate tooling and training, while larger portfolios may benefit from dedicated MLOps specialization.

items.question: What is the difference between MLOps and ModelOps?
items.answer: The terms are often used interchangeably. MLOps is the broader term encompassing the full ML lifecycle. ModelOps sometimes focuses more specifically on the operational aspects of deployed models. In practice, they refer to the same discipline.

items.question: What is a CI/CD pipeline in MLOps?
items.answer: In MLOps, CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment) automates the testing and deployment of model updates — ensuring that model changes can be validated and promoted to production reliably and quickly, similar to software CI/CD but with additional model-specific validation steps.

items.question: How does MLOps handle data versioning?
items.answer: MLOps includes data versioning alongside model versioning — tracking which dataset version was used to train each model. This enables reproduction of training runs and diagnosis of issues when model behavior changes.

items.question: What is the relationship between MLOps and AI governance?
items.answer: MLOps provides the technical infrastructure for AI governance — versioning, monitoring, and documentation. Governance defines the policies; MLOps provides the means to implement and evidence those policies in practice.
